met_analysis:
The Depression over coastal Myanmar and adjoining Northeast Bay of Bengal moved west-northwestwards with a speed of 18 kmph during past 6 hours and lies centered at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 29th September 2026 over coastal Myanmar and adjoining Northeast Bay of Bengal & southeast Bangladesh near latitude 20.7°N and longitude 94.3°E, about 80 km south-southeast of Mindat (Myanmar), 170 km east of Kyauktaw (Myanmar), 260 km east-southeast of Cox’s Bazar (Bangladesh), and 320 km southeast of Chittagong (Bangladesh), 370 km south-southeast of Aizawl (Mizoram, India). It is very likely to move northwestwards and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over coastal Myanmar and adjoining southeast Bangladesh & Northeast Bay of Bengal during next 12 hours. Thereafter, it is very likely to continue to move further northwestwards towards southeast Bangladesh and adjoining areas of Myanmar, Mizoram, Tripura & Northeast Bay of Bengal and weaken gradually during subsequent 24 hours. The line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through 32.5°N/72.5°E, Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa, Naliya and 23.0°N/67.8°E.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Haryana & neighbourhood between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level with a trough aloft in middle and upper tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 72°E to the north of Lat. 25°N persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over East Uttar Pradesh at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over northeast Assam & neighbourhood between 1.5 & 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Northwest & adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Eastcentral Arabian sea between 1.5 & 4.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over north Tamil Nadu & adjoining south Coastal Andhra Pradesh extending upto 1.5 km above mean sea level persists.
The north-south trough from south Telangana to Gulf of Mannar across Rayalaseema & upper air cyclonic circulation over north Tamil Nadu & adjoining south Coastal Andhra Pradesh at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
